record.summary: SB 1119, 'Adam's Law', named after Adam Raine, expands California's child-safety rules for companion chatbots, building on SB 243. It requires age assurance, risk assessments before a new or substantially modified companion chatbot is released, in-app crisis referrals and notice to a parent of a credible threat of self-harm, parent-controlled default settings such as time limits, reasonable measures against harmful outputs such as self-harm, sexually explicit or emotionally manipulative content, an incident reporting mechanism overseen by the Attorney General, limits on targeted advertising to children, and independent compliance audits reported to the Attorney General.
record.notes: Passed the Legislature on 31 Aug 2026 (Senate 39-0, Assembly 64-4) and signed 10 Sep 2026 (Padilla; Wicks; Bauer-Kahan) in a 13-bill child online-safety package that also included SB 867 (toys: companion chatbots), AB 1709 (covered platforms: age restriction) and SB 1276 (crimes: sexual exploitation of a child). It builds on SB 243 (2025), uses the age-bracket signal of AB 1043 (2025) and draws on provisions of AB 1064 (2025) on harmful outputs. It also gives families harmed by violations of its crisis-referral, parental-notice, default-protection and harmful-output provisions a private right of redress.

verification.note: The stored Governor's release of 10 Sep 2026 (copy of 14 Oct 2026; its text matches the 11 Oct copy) confirms the signing of SB 1119, its authors and its listed subject 'Companion chatbots: children's safety', and describes 'Adam's Law'. The stored release of Senator Padilla (31 Aug 2026, sd18.senate.ca.gov) names the bill 'Adam's Law (SB 1119)' and lists its requirements and the floor votes; it describes the version passed by the Legislature, which the Governor then signed. The leginfo.legislature.ca.gov pages for the bill and for Gov. Code sec. 9600 could not be stored, so the bill text, chapter number and effective date are unconfirmed. The record's second stored file (document-1.pdf) is EO N-12-23 of 2023, linked from the release, and is not a source for SB 1119.

judgment.status_reasoning: Events in the stored files: the Legislature passed SB 1119 on 31 Aug 2026 (Padilla release: 'the bill now heads to Governor Gavin Newsom's desk'), and the Governor signed it with the rest of the package on 10 Sep 2026 (release dated 'Sep 10, 2026'; 'With the Governor's signature on these bills'). Neither stored release contains an effective-date or urgency clause. Under California's general rule (Gov. Code sec. 9600; the leginfo page could not be stored), a non-urgency statute enacted in a regular session takes effect on 1 January after a 90-day period from enactment. For a bill enacted on 10 Sep 2026 that is 1 Jan 2027, after today (14 Oct 2026). Status stays 'Adopted, not yet in force'. date_in_force stays null because neither the chaptered text nor the rule could be stored; the chaptered text may also set later operative dates for individual duties.
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope without a scope note: an AI-specific state statute on the safety of companion chatbots for children.
